script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

---

Title: A FRESH START

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

A cheerful SARAH (30s), wearing a flowered apron, prepares breakfast for her two children, LUCY (8) and TOM (5). They share an apartment in the heart of the city.

SARAH:
(talking to herself)
They're growing up so fast. I want to give them the best life possible.

LUCY:
Mom, can I help?

Sarah nods, handing Lucy a bowl to set the table.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Sarah sits at the kitchen table, looking at a stack of job applications and resumes. She wears a determined expression.

Tom enters, holding a drawing.

TOMLIN:
Look what I made, Mom!

Sarah smiles, setting aside her papers.

SARAH:
Wow, Tom, that's fantastic! What is it?

TOMLIN:
It's a drawing of our family. We're happy and safe in our home.

Sarah's eyes fill with tears.

SARAH:
Oh, Tom, that's beautiful. I'll hang it up right away.

INT. SARAH'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

Sarah lies in bed, awake and stressed, with her laptop open. She scrolls through job listings and company websites, searching for the perfect opportunity.

Suddenly, she receives an email notification. Her heart races as she opens it.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Sarah enters the kitchen with a big smile, holding her phone.

SARAH:
Guess what? I got an interview for a marketing position at Sunrise Industries!

The kids jump up and down in excitement.

LUCY:
That's amazing, Mom! We're so proud of you!

SARAH:
Thank you, kids. I couldn't have done it without your support.

INT. SUNRISE INDUSTRIES - WAITING ROOM - DAY

Sarah sits nervously in the waiting room, fidgeting with her purse. She looks at her reflection in the polished tabletop, smoothing her hair and composing herself.

Suddenly, a MRS. SULLIVAN (50s), wearing a business suit, enters the room and takes a seat beside Sarah. They exchange friendly smiles.

MRS. SULLIVAN:
You look nervous. It's your first interview, isn't it?

SARAH:
Yes, it is. I've been out of the workforce for a while, and I'm trying to get back in.

Mrs. Sullivan leans in, offering words of encouragement.

MRS. SULLIVAN:
You'll do great. Just be yourself and show them your passion and dedication.

INT. SUNRISE INDUSTRIES - INTERVIEW ROOM - DAY

Sarah enters the interview room, where she meets MR. O'BRIEN (40s), the hiring manager. They exchange pleasantries, and Sarah begins to answer his questions.

MR. O'BRIEN:
So, why do you want to work for Sunrise Industries?

SARAH:
I believe in your mission to create eco-friendly products and make a positive impact on the world. I want to be a part of that and contribute my skills to help grow the company.

Mr. O'Brien is impressed by her passion and enthusiasm. The interview continues, with Sarah acing each question.

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

Sarah returns home, beaming with excitement. She shares the news with her children, who celebrate with her.

SARAH:
I got the job, kids! I'm going to start working at Sunrise Industries next week!

Tom and Lucy cheer and hug their mother.

INT. SUNRISE INDUSTRIES - OFFICE - DAY

Sarah settles into her new office, surrounded by her coworkers. She feels a renewed sense of purpose and pride.

SARAH:
(to herself)
I did it. A fresh start for my family and me.

EXT. SCHOOL - AFTERNOON

Sarah waits for Tom and Lucy outside their school, wearing a proud smile.

TOM:
Mom, can we go to the park and play after school?

SARAH:
Of course, Tom. And, Lucy, how about we make dinner tonight? You can help me cook.

They all share excited smiles and head off to the park.

FADE OUT.

---

This screenplay focuses on the theme of second chances and the importance of a fresh start. The story revolves around a mother, Sarah, who is determined to give her children the best life possible while trying to get back into the workforce. With no guns, violence, or copyrighted characters, this modern family screenplay is a heartwarming and uplifting tale of perseverance and love.
